key.name: kinetic-scrolling
key.description:
Controls gtk_scrolled_window_set_kinetic_scrolling on the document scrolled window. When true (default), trackpad flicks coast and diagonal trackpad gestures pan in both axes simultaneously — the standard GTK behavior. When false, scroll events apply only the user-induced delta with no momentum, and diagonal motion is delivered to GTK as paired axis events.
The earlier default-false rationale (cap input to keep the render cache from outrunning) is obsolete since v0.14 introduced GThreadPool sort-function priority dispatch and v0.17 added fz_cookie mid-render abort: the cache responds to scroll velocity without needing an input-side cap.

key.name: reading-ruler
key.description: When true, dim the page everywhere except a horizontal band that tracks the mouse cursor. Useful for dense technical reading where keeping your eye on the active line is the failure mode. Toggleable from the primary menu; the setting persists across sessions.

key.name: loupe
key.summary: Show a magnifying loupe at the cursor
key.description: When true, render a circular zoomed view of the underlying page content centered on the mouse cursor. Useful for dense comic panels, small chart axis labels, and footnote text on scanned documents. The magnification factor is fixed at 2.5×. Toggleable from the primary menu or via F7; the setting persists.

key.name: crop-margins
key.summary: Auto-crop whitespace margins from PDF pages
key.description: When true, scan the current visible page's text via the cached structured-text page, compute the content bounding box, and apply the resulting margin fractions uniformly across the document. Pages render without their whitespace margins so the text occupies more of the screen — useful on small laptop screens with dense technical PDFs. Has no effect on backends that don't support stext-based content detection (DjVu, CBR). Toggleable from the primary menu or via F6; the setting persists.
